name: Orukeet (Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 with Gabor encoder filters)
vendor: Oruk AI (with Stanford, Cambridge, OpenWhispr, Hoid authors)

lineage.how_derived: replaces half of the encoder's temporal depthwise filters with 12,288 fitted frozen Gabor kernels, then trains the remaining parameters on multilingual, multi-accent data (finetune per card)

purpose: Multilingual (25 languages) speech recogniser for recordings, media, batch transcription, server workers and interactive applications, outperforming Parakeet v3 (card).

license.name: Weights CC-BY-SA-4.0, code MIT
license.notes: LICENSE-WEIGHTS (header 'Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International') and LICENSE (MIT, Knuckles92 2025 / Oruk AI 2026) opened, not read in full. ShareAlike: derivatives of the weights must carry CC BY-SA 4.0 (fine-tunes and conversions published by us would too).

architecture.kind: FastConformer (24 layers, hidden 1024, 8 heads, 8x subsampling) + 2-layer TDT decoder, durations 0-4, vocab 8193

variants.notes: also Transformers export at the repo root
plus Core ML zips of 0.47-0.55 GB

engine_support.notes: The GGUF files are for the project's own transcribe.cpp runtime, not llama.cpp (card tag transcribe_cpp).

benchmarks.name: LibriSpeech test-clean / test-other WER
benchmarks.variant: Orukeet (parakeet v3: 1.53 / 3.14); checkpoint selection used test-other

strengths: Better than Parakeet v3 on 61 of 74 tested splits (card)
many ready runtimes (ONNX, GGUF, Core ML)
weaknesses: checkpoint selected on LibriSpeech test-other, which the card also reports
soft.maturity: Small company plus university authors; technical report PDF in the repo.

tona_fit.reason: Drop-in improvement over Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 for 25 languages including German at the same size (0.6B, 0.7 GB at Q8); fits every class. Verify the German WER ourselves (the card gives pooled FLEURS only in the text I read) before replacing the parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 record as the offer. ShareAlike applies to anything we redistribute.

sources.note: README, config.json, HF API file list

open_questions: German-only FLEURS WER not extracted (per-language table not read)
